small_guidance:
- The fused tail kernel is fine; the bottleneck is the torch ConvTranspose3d (stride=1, padding=1, kernel=3 → output is the same spatial shape as input). Tuning BLOCK_HW/num_warps in the tail won't move fast_p; leave it at BLOCK_HW=128/256, num_warps=8, num_stages=2.
- If staying with torch conv, at least switch to channels_last_3d memory format and run conv in fp32 with cudnn benchmark enabled to get the best cuDNN algo selected.
- Make sure the tail kernel reads `x` with stride awareness (or `.contiguous()` only once) so it doesn't force an extra layout copy after conv.
large_guidance:
- Replace the ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton kernel. Since stride=1, padding=1, kernel=3, ConvTranspose3d here is equivalent in shape to a regular Conv3d with the flipped kernel — implement it as a direct gather-style conv (one program per (N, OC tile, D*H*W tile)) doing a GEMM over (IC*kd*kh*kw). Output D=32, H=W=128, OC=64 — plenty of parallelism.
- Fuse the depth-mean reduction directly into the conv epilogue: each program accumulates over its assigned output (h,w) tile by looping kd and d, dividing by D at the end — this avoids materializing the full (B,64,32,128,128) tensor (~256 MB) which dominates memory traffic.
- After the depth-fused conv, run the existing softmax/tanh/scale kernel on the (B,C,1,H,W) tensor — or fuse it too if the per-(b,h,w) channel vector (C=64) fits in registers, giving a single-pass kernel from input to final output.
